## Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata 

March 3, 1839 to May 19, 1904 

December 28, 1937 to October 9, 2024 

In a free enterprise, the community is not just another stakeholder in business, but is in fact the very purpose of its existence. 

It is with a profound sense of loss that we bid farewell to Mr. Ratan Naval Tata, a truly uncommon leader whose immeasurable contributions have shaped not only the Tata Group but also the very fabric of our nation. 

For the Tata Group, Mr. Tata was more than a chairperson. He inspired by example. With an unwavering commitment to excellence, integrity and innovation, the Tata Group under his stewardship expanded its global footprint while always remaining true to its moral compass. 

Mr. Tata’s dedication to philanthropy and the development of society has touched the lives of millions. From education to healthcare, his initiatives have left a deep-rooted mark that will benefit generations to come. Reinforcing all of this work was Mr. Tata’s genuine humility in every individual interaction. 

His legacy will continue to inspire us as we strive to uphold the principles he so passionately championed. 

In this Report 

Integrate. Uncomplicate. Innovate. 

**Imagine a world** …where a cement manufacturer aims to reduce its carbon footprint and meet its sustainability targets with agility. A shipping company wants to cut down its operating costs substantially. An aviation company seeks to achieve always-on, anywhere-on connectivity for its crew. 

At Tata Communications, our Digital Fabric aims to remove these roadblocks by offering a unified platform that simplifies management, enhances visibility and provides a secure foundation for building hyperconnected ecosystems. 

Given the complexity around lack of omnichannel consistency, need to deploy solutions across technologies, privacy concerns etc., coupled with the customer's requirement to be future ready, our Digital Fabric provides Real-time, Alwayson, Anywhere-on, Seamlessly Collaborative, Integrated Data Analytics and Intelligence, helping our customers stay ahead of the curve. 

None of these milestones would be possible for the enterprises, without the support of a strong digital foundation —one that underpins everything from cloud infrastructure and network operations to delivering exceptional customer experiences, powered by AI and Innovations. 

The global business landscape is undergoing a radical shift, with new challenges and opportunities emerging on the horizon. Delivering a seamless experience is not easy as enterprises face the challenges of integrating and managing a complex array of technologies, often with a mix of legacy tools and infrastructure. Moreover, data silos, fragmented systems and disparate processes make it difficult for them to deliver omnichannel, contextual interactions. Add to it the ever-increasing security and privacy concerns. 

Our digital fabric brings together tools and expertise that can help businesses simplify large digital infrastructure, uncomplicate their IT estate and provide more visibility and control across various infrastructure systems including network, cloud and security. It facilitates the exchange of data, information and intelligence across diverse digital systems and applications. 

**By focusing on a strong digital foundation, global businesses can navigate headwinds and set the stage for future growth and innovation.**

Why Tata Communications? 

# **Because evolved hyperconnected ecosystems is the future** 

From the convergence of media to AI powered customer engagement, from the rise of hybrid workplaces to the acceleration of borderless commerce, enterprises today demand scale, agility, intelligence and seamless integration. We stand at the confluence of these transformative shifts – driving strategic expansion, sustained growth and responsible operations. 

Our strategy is shaped by this evolving enterprise landscape, where integration and intelligence are no longer optional but foundational. Guided by disciplined capital allocation, platform integration and a purpose-led approach to growth, we are executing with clarity and conviction. Our ambition to double data revenue is built around a multi-dimensional scale – expanding enterprise relevance while staying true to responsible business principles. We are strengthening digital infrastructure, accelerating the integration of acquisitions and capturing the full potential of cloud, AI and IoT. 

With a future-ready Digital Fabric, deep domain expertise, and a trusted global presence, Tata Communications is the partner of choice for enterprises navigating the next frontier of digital transformation. 



## **Global leadership in digital infrastructure solutions** 

We are providing seamless, high-speed and secure connectivity across the globe through our extensive network and agile digital infrastructure. We have the ability to connect cloud to cloud, data centre to cloud, user to cloud as well as within and across cloud in minutes, with a superior customer experience. 

## **Acquisitions accelerate capability enhancements** 

Our recent acquisitions, which include The Switch and Kaleyra, have strategically expanded our reach and product offerings. The Switch enhanced our production capabilities and presence in North American media and entertainment market, while Kaleyra strengthened our Customer Interaction portfolio capabilities. These integrations aim to increase revenue and leverage our infrastructure. 

## **Rising data revenue share, growing relevance** 

Data drives 84% of our revenue, validating our transformation into a digital solutions provider. Our enterprise customers are investing in cloud, security, next-gen connectivity, Media and IoT solutions, which are cumulatively driving the expansion of our digital portfolio. The digital portfolio comprises 47% of our data revenue and is growing significantly (21.4% CAGR) since FY 19-20. 

## **A healthy order book, with a growing funnel** 

We have a healthy order book with a robust funnel driven by sectoral tailwinds and customer trust. New order wins are well-distributed across verticals, geographies and offerings. The increase in order book is owing to our continuous investment in portfolio expansion and capacity expansion of our sales division. This diversity, combined with long-term contracts and customer loyalty, provides stable revenue and sustainable growth. 

## **Led by experience, built for scale** 

Leadership continuity has been vital in powering our transformation journey. Our management team brings domain expertise, execution focus and a shared vision for a sustained future. Powered by a proven track record of delivering on capital allocation, integration and profitable growth, the leadership team has consistently balanced ambition with a disciplined approach. The stewardship has been vital in reshaping our portfolio and instilling a performance-led culture. 

## **Sustainable by design** 

We are building a digital future that is inclusive, responsible and climate-conscious. Our commitment to be Net Zero by 2035 is backed by measurable actions, including reductions in Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, increased use of renewable energy and investments in green infrastructure. ESG principles are embedded across our supply chain, governance practices and portfolio innovation. Our approach to sustainability is strategically aligned with customer expectations and long-term stakeholder value.

# Letter from the Chairman 

Moderate global growth, changes in the geopolitical scenario, including tariffs worldwide and uncertainties surrounding sanctions, pose challenges. Your Company continues to navigate these challenges and remains resilient. While these tariffs may impact IT spending for our customers, the Company is confident in overcoming these obstacles through the value additions it has demonstrated to its customers across all its fabrics. 

**I believe that we are well-placed to lead in India and compete globally. Our focus on innovation, putting customers first and building a sustainable future will continue to shape our journey ahead. As we look forward, I am confident in our ability to drive meaningful impact and unlock longterm value for all our stakeholders.**

Enterprises today need secure, flexible networks that can adapt to evolving business demands and ensure seamless user experiences. The shift to hybrid cloud, rising compliance needs, and the growth of AI, IoT, and edge technologies are accelerating demand for advanced cloud networking and digital transformation solutions. Tata Communications’ product and services portfolio delivers curated and effective solutions that address these client needs. 

Your Company’s progress rests on strategic investments in technology, partnerships and sustainability.

Your Company’s robust digital fabric combines infrastructure, platforms and services through an orchestration and management layer that enables enterprises to uncomplicate their digital infrastructure, transform their cost structure and unlock new growth avenues. We are well-positioned to drive digital transformation for enterprises with Innovation, AI, Automation and Sustainability built into our business model.

### Message from MD and CEO 

# **Sustaining our growth momentum** 

**Your Company is enabling enterprises worldwide by providing secure, agile and scalable digital infrastructure solutions. With global network accessibility from over 190 countries and territories, your Company is well-positioned to drive digital transformation for enterprises.** 

#### **Dear Shareholders,** 

It is my privilege to present Tata Communications’ Integrated Annual Report for the financial year 24-25. As we reflect on the year, I am proud of the progress we have made in delivering innovation, resilience and sustainable growth, despite global macroeconomic uncertainties and shifting global trade dynamics. As the world continues to redefine the boundaries of connectivity and intelligence, Tata Communications has moved forward with purpose, strengthening our position as the digital fabric of enterprises around the globe. Notwithstanding the operational headwinds and potential delays in enterprise decisionmaking, our differentiated digital fabric continues to reinforce our relevance to customers positioning us well for FY 25-26 and beyond. 



##### **Accelerating strategic transformation** 

In FY 24-25, we advanced our vision of enabling hyperconnected ecosystems with a sharp focus on financial fitness and deepening our capabilities in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, IoT and next-generation connectivity. Our commitment to driving value creation has been reflected in our financial performance. 

A key highlight of the year was robust growth in our digital portfolio revenue, maintaining strong momentum over the past two years. Our Enterprise revenue from both the domestic and international markets also saw good YoY growth. Our order book has grown significantly YoY, and is now well diversified, reflecting our successful transformation over time. 

During the year, our consolidated revenue from operations reached `H` 23,109 crore, reflecting a 11.2% year-on-year growth. Our data revenue, which forms the backbone of our business, grew by 13.7% YoY to `H` 19,513 crore, while digital portfolio revenue surged by 29.5% YoY. 

Our strategic interventions, including the divestment of non-core assets such as Tata Communications Payment Solutions Limited, land parcel monetisation at Ambattur and enhanced subsidiary profitability, have strengthened our balance sheet and sharpened our focus on highgrowth areas. These efforts reduced our net debt-toEBITDA ratio to 2.06x, nearing our goal of below 2x.

## Network Fabric 

In FY 24-25, our Network Fabric, encompassing core and next-generation connectivity, delivered a robust performance. Driven by strong demand for data centre-to-data centre (DC-to-DC) connectivity, we achieved a steady year-on-year revenue growth of 3.2%. Our next-generation connectivity portfolio recorded an impressive 13.4% year-on-year growth, with our IZO<sup>TM</sup> Hybrid WAN and IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi-Cloud Connect solutions driving large-scale network transformations. The latter achieved a revenue CAGR of over 50% over the past three years, securing strategic contracts across BFSI, automotive and airline sectors. Our transformation of the Tier 1 network into a software-defined, AI-enabled platform with 99.8% first-time-right deployments and 95%+ proactive fault diagnosis has strengthened our global scale, delivering predictable performance and SLAs across 150 countries. 

## Interaction Fabric 

The Interaction fabric, which includes collaboration and managed Communications Platform as a Service ('CPaaS') solutions, experienced a 51.9% growth aided by inorganic investments. Throughout the year, we expanded our offerings to include programmable voice, video, Rich Communication Services ('RCS'), and WhatsApp channels, while investing in channel and customer journey orchestration, boosting interaction intelligence through our Kaleyra.ai platform. 

## Cloud Fabric 

The Cloud fabric delivered an impressive 10.5% yearon-year revenue growth for the year, driven primarily by a major contract announced earlier in the year. Our security offerings have seen a strong order book, particularly in the BFSI sector. 

## IoT Fabric 

Our IoT fabric, an incubation portfolio, achieved a remarkable 41.6% year-on-year revenue growth in FY 24-25. This was driven by the addition of new vehicles to our platform and a significant increase in data usage on our Tata Communications MOVE<sup>TM</sup> platform. These developments are encouraging indicators of our strategy to drive platform growth in this segment. 

## Media and Entertainment Portfolio Success 

The media portfolio recorded a 4.1% growth yearon-year in FY 24-25. Our partnership with World 



Athletics was another defining moment for us last year. As part of this, Tata Communications will manage broadcast operations and production for all World Athletics events from 2025 to 2029, kicking off with the Indoor Championships in Nanjing and the prestigious World Championships in Tokyo. With this partnership, we aim to enhance the fan experience, making every jump, sprint and marathon more accessible and engaging to audiences worldwide. 

# **Embedding AI at the core of our business** 

We are embedding Artificial Intelligence at the core of our business to unlock transformative value across innovation, customer experience and operational efficiency. We view AI not just as a tool for operational efficiency but as a strategic lever to drive innovation, enhance customer experience and unlock new growth opportunities. By infusing AI at all levels of digital fabric, we are accelerating growth and unlocking new possibilities. Our AI Centre of Excellence is driving the adoption of AI across products, platforms and internal processes, while our AI Academy is upskilling talent across business units to deliver high-impact, domain-specific use cases. We are also working with ecosystem partners to bring diverse AI-powered solutions to the market. With AI-led innovations in areas such as Conversational AI for customer interactions and network security, we are not only transforming how we work but also helping enterprises unlock new value from their digital investments. 

# **Unlocking value through strategic acquisitions** 

Our strategic acquisitions prior to FY 24-25 are yielding significant benefits. The integration of Kaleyra into our CIS business has been seamless and with the launch of Kaleyra.ai, we are enabling enterprises enhance customer communications through AI- powered workflows and templates. Kaleyra has also expanded its footprint, acquiring new customers in the UK and Europe, including leading enterprises across geographies. 

Similarly, The Switch has been successfully integrated into our Media and Entertainment Business, securing significant customers in the US college sports, e-sports and global video provider segments, further strengthening our global presence. 

# **Building a Responsible Company** 

Tata Communications' sustainability strategy focuses on three pillars viz., People, Planet and Community. This strategy is centered around robust corporate 

governance and aims to create long-term stakeholder value and sustainable growth. The Company emphasises its commitment to social well-being, environmental stewardship, community engagement and ethical governance, aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the Tata Group Sustainability Strategy. 

Your Company also helps create sustainable livelihoods, supporting women and underserved young citizens with skills training and entrepreneurship opportunities across various regions. These initiatives are aligned with the Tata Group’s ethos of trust and responsibility. 

In today’s fast-moving world, it is essential for your Company to build a workplace where diversity and inclusion thrive. That is how we stay agile and innovative. We also place strong emphasis on supporting our people’s growth—through focused training and leadership programmes that not only attract top talent but also create a culture where everyone can learn, lead and succeed together. 

# **Enabling an exciting and empowering future** 

Our execution remains robust as ever, reflected in our digital data growth, combined with rising revenues and increased cash flow. We are committed to adding value to our customers by empowering them to navigate their hyperconnected ecosystems with confidence. Looking ahead, we will sharpen our focus on staying relevant by investing in innovative product offerings and expanding our portfolio in step with evolving customer needs. 

We are truly honoured for the recognition that we received this year. We won the prestigious JRD QV Award under the category of ‘Industry Leader’, a reflection of our pursuit of quality, innovation and the Tata values that inspire and guide us. We were also recognised across key domains by analysts including Gartner, IDC, ISG, Juniper Research and Frost & Sullivan during the year. These included leadership positions in global WAN, UCaaS, SD-WAN, IoT and CPaaS. These honours signal the growing relevance of our platforms and the value we deliver to our customers worldwide. 

As businesses around the world reinvent themselves, the need for them to invest in robust and secure digital infrastructure remains critical—even in the face of global macro headwinds. Tata Communications is well-positioned to be their trusted partner in 

this transformation. We will continue to invest in strengthening our product portfolio and embedding AI to power intelligent, future-ready solutions. Our sharpened sales and marketing efforts have yielded tangible outcomes, with a steady rise in million-dollar customers over the past five years, a momentum we are focused on accelerating across both India and international markets. Internally, we are simplifying our processes and leveraging AI to drive operational efficiency and deliver richer customer experiences. As we grow, we remain deeply committed to our ESG goals—advancing environmental sustainability, social equity and good governance. A special highlight this year has been the phenomenal volunteering efforts of our employees, which earned us the prestigious Tata Engage Award. This is a true testament to our culture of purpose and community impact, and we will continue to focus on expanding our efforts to give back to society. 

We remain committed to staying ahead of the technology curve, with the support of our customers, colleagues, partners, investors and the wider stakeholder fraternity. Your trust in our vision and capabilities fuels our ability to create amplified value in the emerging digital era.

## Network Fabric 

Tata Communications’ Network Fabric is a composable, high-speed, on-demand and intent-based platform. We are revolutionising network management through advanced AI and analytics. By embedding these powerful capabilities, we provide predictive and proactive assurance processes, allowing us to anticipate and resolve potential issues before impacting customer operations. ## Tata Communications Vayu Cloud* 

Tata Communications Vayu Cloud is a unified, high-performance platform that seamlessly connects cloud to edge, data to AI and security to connectivity, eliminating complexity across the enterprise. Purpose-built for agility and efficiency, it enables frictionless data movement, real-time insights and effortless technology integration. With end-to-end tools for data management, experimentation, training, fine-tuning and deployment, Tata Communications Vayu Cloud harmonises data, tools and AI workflows while ensuring consistent performance across centralised and decentralised environments.

## Tata Communications Vayu Edge*

Expertly managed and highly secure, it enables seamless deployment and management of applications anywhere, backed by nearzero downtime assurance. It supports the deployment of AI models and algorithms at the edge, enabling local processing and inference. Offering a comprehensive solution that spans edge infrastructure, platform, network, managed services and industry-specific use cases, Tata Communications Vayu Edge empowers realtime analytics and decision-making at the edge. It unlocks new possibilities for innovation, helping businesses thrive in a fast-paced, data-driven world.

# **Integrating** 

## Tata Communications Beacon Platform 

AI/ML is already transforming how enterprises orchestrate hybrid infrastructure and Tata Communications Beacon puts that power directly into the hands of operations teams. Instead of drowning in alarms and fragmented dashboards, Tata Communications Beacon uses pattern mining and AI-based correlation to surface the root cause. Built on the pillars of Discoverability, Manageability and Security, it enables Network Agnostic Fault and Performance Prediction across WAN, LAN and wireless environments. 

The platform uses AI/ML based correlation of Network Alarms and uses Sequence Pattern Mining for detecting the zone of fault (overlay or underlay) or predicting the occurrence of fault in advance with greater prediction accuracy and higher coverage. Tata Communications Beacon does not just show what is happening, it can act on it too. The platform democratises AI through its ML Studio interface, enabling customers to accelerate their AI/ML maturity journey and advance towards cognitive network capabilities. With ML Studio interfaces, teams can visualise alarm clusters, predict degradation and trigger auto-resolution workflows without needing a data science background. 



## Interaction Fabric 

## Kaleyra AI 

**Kaleyra AI** is a next-generation platform designed to elevate customer engagement, streamline workflows and unlock strategic insights with the power of Generative AI. It empowers businesses to deliver exceptional, personalised experiences effortlessly—fueling go-to-market strategies and accelerating growth. With AI-driven intelligence at its core, Kaleyra AI transforms every interaction into a meaningful touchpoint, making customer journeys more impactful and memorable. 

The platform simplifies data visualisation by generating dynamic, insightful charts and graphs in seconds, while AI-powered conversations eliminate the manual grind of reporting—saving time and boosting productivity. It offers a unified view of data across all channels, enabling faster, smarter decision-making. With its intuitive no-code interface, users can build conversational assistants in minutes—no technical expertise required. Just upload your files, and the assistant is ready to deliver accurate, business-specific responses in a natural, conversational tone.

## AI Driven Use-cases 

Our IoT fabric seamlessly integrates sensor data across multi-network environments through a robust IoT platform, forming the essential data backbone for AI and analytics. This plug-and-play solution enables effortless remote monitoring, realtime visibility, and intelligent control of connected devices. With scalable device management, APIbased application integration, and a powerful analytics engine, it empowers faster, smarter decision-making. Supporting a growing suite of AIdriven use cases focused on safety and security, the platform enables applications such as asset tracking, smart lighting control, temperature and humidity monitoring and diesel generator performance management.

# Financial 

Strategy Fuelling Resilient Growth 

With our strong business fundamentals, we have implemented multiple strategic measures to expand our capacity for future opportunities and realign our assets for long-term, profitable growth. 



Our financial strategy is built to deliver sustainable growth, resilient performance and long-term shareholder value. Anchored in the Fit to Grow and Fit to Compete frameworks, we continue to strengthen our balance sheet, optimise capital deployment and drive disciplined expansion. Strategic investments in digital infrastructure, product innovation and operational efficiency position us to scale with speed while maintaining robust return ratios and enhancing capital productivity. This approach ensures we remain agile, competitive and well-positioned to generate attractive returns for our investors.

Financial discipline remains central to our growth strategy. Through efficient capital allocation, streamlined operations and improved cashflow visibility, we have built a strong financial framework to support business growth and reinvestment. 

**Our structured approach**<sup>_</sup> featuring zero-based budgeting, proactive working capital management and strategic asset monetisation ensures capital is allocated effectively towards high-growth areas. A balanced debt portfolio, aligned with our interest rate hedging strategy, improves financial stability by mitigating market risks and optimising cost structures. 

With resilient cash flow management, we continue to prioritise liquidity and capital efficiency to fund innovation, expansion and long-term value creation. 

### **Investing in Innovation and Infrastructure** 

To support this disciplined financial approach, we are making targeted investments in cable systems and underlay maintenance, ensuring the reliability and scalability of our core infrastructure. Simultaneously, we are expanding our global connectivity solutions to meet growing demand, particularly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Our focus on AI-driven solutions and hyperconnected networks is enabling the development of intelligent, real-time and seamless digital experiences. These investments are critical to enhancing service delivery, expanding market reach and positioning us for longterm leadership in a hyperconnected world.

These initiatives aim to realign our asset base, improve resource utilisation and support investments in growth areas—helping to gradually strengthen profitability alongside revenue. 

Together, these efforts reflect a dual approach to growth— **organic** , through internal efficiencies and strategic focus and **inorganic** , through asset optimisation and portfolio realignment—ensuring a resilient and scalable path to sustained profitability. 

# **Strategic Expansion through M&A** 

Our mergers and acquisitions ('M&A') approach is guided by a flexible framework that prioritises strategic alignment over fixed predefined targets. We evaluate inorganic opportunities based on their ability to: 

- Expand our product portfolio 

- Broaden our geographic footprint 

- Strengthen our market position 

These principles have consistently shaped our recent acquisitions of Kaleyra, The Switch and Oasis, ensuring alignment with our long-term growth objectives and value creation goals. 

The acquisitions of Kaleyra and The Switch have boosted digital services to over 47% of overall data revenues, aligning with our medium-term growth goals. These integrations unlock new customer segments, enhance product capabilities, improve cross-selling potential and increase enterprise wallet share.

## **Next-Gen Connectivity** 

We enable businesses to navigate through their digital transformation needs with scalable, on-demand, agile and multi-cloud enabled solutions. 

### **High-impact advancements in FY 24-25** 

#### IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Connect 

We introduced IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Connect Network Hub and VNFaaS (VNF as a Service) to address customers’ multi-cloud, large and complex cloud landing zone problem. 

#### IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Network 

We introduced a full-stack cloud networking solution called IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Network, which includes IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Connect and IZO<sup>TM</sup> Multi Cloud Network ensuring seamless cloud access, frictionless application management and granular security.

At Tata Communications, we aim to transform refreshing new ideas into impactful business outcomes through open innovation that blends internal ideation, external partnerships and rigorous evaluation. #### **Mapping ‘Jobs’ to ‘Capabilities’** 

Our innovation initiatives are strategically driven to support business goals. The Corporate Venturing and Innovations Group ('CVIG') spearheads the Open Innovation programmes. The CVIG curates a portfolio of initiatives, such as AI-driven projects and solution to emerging customer challenges, leveraging the power of technology to build capabilities across products, services, processes and people. These initiatives are strategically aligned with evolving customer needs, emerging markets, new consumption models and platform developments.

## **Our Commitment to Business Human Rights** 

Tata Communications is firmly committed to respecting and promoting human rights across its operations and value chain. Our Business & Human Rights (‘BHR’) Policy, approved by the MD and CEO and available on our website, addresses key issues such as anti-discrimination, fair wages, digital rights and modern slavery, aligned with internal policies and processes. The CSR, Safety and Sustainability Committee exercises oversight over the BHR Policy and was apprised of the BHR gap assessment findings and the related action plan during FY 24-25. 

In FY 24-25, ESG assessments, conducted in partnership with EcoVadis, covered 55% of our key suppliers, enabling targeted improvement plans. 

We also expanded our Supplier Diversity Programme, onboarding four new suppliers from underrepresented communities and launching a Diversity Questionnaire and awareness workshops to build their capabilities and inclusion in our sourcing ecosystem. 

In FY 24-25, we began annual UNGC Communication on Progress submissions, reinforcing our commitment to its Ten Principles. We also updated our Modern Slavery Statement in line with the UK Act, affirming zero cases for forced, child labour and trafficking this year. Two targeted sessions were also held for suppliers on responsible business practices and grievance mechanisms. 

We uphold zero tolerance for malpractice and human rights violations. A comprehensive grievance mechanism— including a robust Whistleblower Policy and independent Ethics Helpline—enables confidential, retaliation-free reporting by employees and stakeholders. No significant human rights grievances were reported during FY 24-25.

We have embedded human rights into supplier engagement through our Supplier Code of Conduct, which forms an integral part of business agreements. A revised ESG Due Diligence Checklist — (for suppliers crossing an identified value threshold) ensures alignment with expectations on labour rights, ethics and sustainability. 

These efforts reflect our ongoing commitment to fostering a safe, ethical and inclusive workplace that upholds human rights at every level.

Jayanti Devi<br><!-- End of picture text -->

**"I thought I wouldn't be able to do it-but I did. Today, I am not only providing for my family, but also building a better future for my daughters and my community." - Jayanti Devi** 

For Jayanti Devi from Periyardha village, life took an unexpected and devastating turn when her husband passed away. His prolonged illness had drained all their savings, leaving Jayanti with the heavy responsibility of raising five children on her own. In 2016, hope arrived when Project MPowered's team conducted a participatory rural appraisal with the community members in the village to identify vulnerable families for inclusion in the project, supported by Tata Communications and implemented by Trickle Up India Foundation. Through the project, Jayanti was introduced to the concept of Self-Help Groups. She joined a group, opened her first bank account and started saving regularly. She also received training in livestock management and sustainable farming practices from Smart Sakhis and the field staff. With financial aid from the project, she bought a goat and began cultivating vegetables on her small piece of land. Determined to build a stable future, she secured a loan from her SHG, expanded her vegetable farming and started selling her produce in the local market even attending up to three haats (local markets) per week. Her goat-rearing business also flourished, adding another source of income. Technology also became a game-changer for her. Through the project, Jayanti received a smartphone-a tool she initially found intimidating but soon mastered. Now, she uses it to access farming tutorials on the PoP (Package of Practices) App to further improve her agricultural techniques. 

Jayanti's success story does not end just with her personal achievements. Alongside nine other women from her village, she started a muri (puffed rice) business as part of a collective enterprise. The group's shared success stands as a powerful symbol of how collective strength and empowerment can drive sustainable change.

#### **Bringing Light, Changing Lives: Solar Power Transforms Chasikgindam** 

In the quiet village of Chasikgindam, a quiet revolution is underway—one powered not by grand gestures, but by sunlight. For Banio Sangma and his family, the shift has been nothing short of life-changing. Six years ago, Banio moved to Waru Songital with his family dreaming of a peaceful life. But that dream was dimmed—literally—by the absence of electricity. Like many others in the village, the Sangmas relied heavily on kerosene and candles, spending a large chunk of their income on temporary light. Many nights were spent huddled around a bonfire, and some dinners passed in darkness, stealing away the warmth of shared moments. 

That changed through the Climate Resilient Village Programme, when Banio’s household received a solar energy kit setup. A seemingly simple setup, yet it brought profound change. The benefits go beyond lighting. Evenings, once constrained by darkness, are now filled with quiet joy—reading books, completing chores and savoring the comfort of a well-lit home. Freed from the financial burden of kerosene, the **"Now, our lives are very different from before”** family can now redirect their resources toward other **-  Banio** essentials, building a brighter and more secure future.

### **The** 

# **TAAP** Vision 

The Tata Affirmative Action Programme envisions creating equitable opportunities for communities through focused initiatives in employment, education, employability and entrepreneurship 

We approach affirmative action with a focus on tangible inclusion, extending opportunities in skill-building, entrepreneurship and livelihoods to communities historically excluded from formal economic and social systems. 

Our programme design takes into account regional disparities, particularly within Marginalised Women, Scheduled Castes ('SCs'), Scheduled Tribes ('STs') and Persons with Disabilities ('PwDs'). We also recognise that caste-based disadvantage often intersects with other forms of marginalisation. For example, women in these communities experience reduced access not only due to gender but also entrenched caste hierarchies. 

We prioritise interventions that apply our core strength— digital solutions—to bridge systemic gaps. By integrating technology into skill development and livelihood 

programmes, we create pathways that are scalable and aligned with future-of-work trends. 

Through TAAP, we go beyond the one-size-fits-all model. Each intervention reflects local realities and each partnership is selected for its ability to unlock long-term potential within marginalised communities.

### **Climate Action and Energy Management** 

We are addressing climate action by reducing emissions within our operations through measurable targets and initiatives. In parallel, we provide training and technical support to suppliers to help lower emissions across the value chain. Additionally, we are expanding our portfolio of products and platforms designed to assist customers in achieving their decarbonisation objectives. 

We operationalise our climate strategy through eight climate levers, tracked via the internal Sustainability Development Committee and integrated into corporate KPIs. Progress is reviewed quarterly, allowing for course corrections based on site-level data to ensure that emission reduction initiatives stay on track.

#### **Decarbonising value chain-based emissions** 

We have moved beyond supplier compliance to supplier capacity building. Our Supply Chain Climate Action Framework addresses the emissions profile of our upstream partners. It is designed to integrate climate performance into procurement governance while establishing our role to influence and engage with suppliers in transforming our supply chain. Under this framework, we aim to work with responsible suppliers and contribute positively to our climate action goal of Net Zero by 2035. The intended result of this framework is for our suppliers to complete their GHG inventory, respond to CDP and formulate science-based emission reduction targets. 

Environmental KPIs represent a part of our Supplier Code of Conduct, with clear mandates for suppliers to disclose emissions through CDP disclosure, commitment to science-based targets and build GHG inventories that act as reference points for emission reduction roadmaps.

#### **Reducing Emissions in Customer Operations (Scope 4)** 

We contribute to wider decarbonisation by embedding low-carbon design across all components of our digital fabric and delivering solutions which enable our customers to avoid GHG emissions. These avoided emissions are measured using internationally aligned protocols. 



We have set a target to achieve avoided GHG emissions (Scope 4) at the customer end equivalent to 20 times of our total GHG emissions (Scope 1, 2, and 3) by FY 26-27. To ensure a robust tracking mechanism, we undertook a comprehensive reassessment of our Low Carbon Products Methodology to prepare it in accordance with GHG Protocol, the Avoided Emissions Framework by Net-Zero Climate Innovation Initiative and with references from the Global enabling Sustainability Initiatives resources. In FY 23-24, 7 of our products, platforms and services enabled avoidance of 3,457,749 MTCO₂e for our customers - equivalent to 14 times of our operational footprint. 

##### Community-based Carbon Offset Initiatives 

We approach offsetting through initiatives that deliver community-level impact. Our Smart Cookstoves Programme, registered under Verra’s Verified Carbon Standard, has helped cut household emissions, while improving daily life for families in underserved regions such as Jharkhand, Odisha and Meghalaya. Total beneficiaries are 14,000 households under this programme. 

By reducing biomass dependence, the programme contributes to better indoor air quality and household health. The resulting carbon credits are fully traceable and aligned with recognised voluntary offset markets. 

Our afforestation and horticulture project in Maharashtra also enhances carbon sinks through native tree planting, while providing employment and training opportunities for local communities covering 500 acres of land. These two initiatives, complementary in their impact, are pivotal to our carbon neutrality strategy.

## **Our Water Stewardship Initiatives for Communities** 

## **Water Stewardship** 

At Tata Communications, our dedication to water stewardship extends far beyond the boundaries of our own operations. As we strive towards becoming a Water Neutral company, we are committed to creating lasting, positive impacts on water availability in local communities across India through meaningful projects: 

Tata Communications recognises water as a vital, limited, and shared resource, and is firmly committed to its sustainable management across all operations. As part of our environmental stewardship, we implement comprehensive measures to optimise water usage, including effective recycling, reuse practices and stringent leakage control at all major facilities. Regular internal audits are conducted to assess and enhance operational efficiency, while targeted training programs and awareness initiatives are carried out to engage stakeholders on the importance of responsible water use and conservation. Our strategic interventions such as wastewater recycling, deployment of rainwater harvesting systems and adoption of innovative technologies like IoT-enabled water meters, have significantly reduced our overall water consumption. We remain focused on continuously identifying and leveraging advanced solutions to further improve water efficiency and ensure long-term sustainability across our facilities. 

### **Chennai, Tamil Nadu:** 

Since 2022, we have partnered with local stakeholders to rejuvenate Nagan Thangal lake in Chennai. This initiative has significantly enhanced the lake’s water holding capacity and groundwater recharge. Additionally, the project has revitalised local biodiversity and transformed the lake into a vibrant community space, welcoming families for recreation and learning – where water and people flourish together. 

### **Dharashiv, Maharashtra:** 

We are working with local partners on integrated watershed development to restore canals and ponds and construct check dams. These interventions are improving water retention, raising ground water levels and enhancing soil fertility thereby ensuring reliable irrigation and supporting sustainable agriculture and rural livelihoods. 



Recycled water usage increased from **16%** to **21%** 



Deployment of rainwater harvesting structures at high-consumption sites resulted in the reusing **3,496KL** of rainwater within our facilities 

Through these projects, Tata Communications is not only working towards water neutrality but also fostering stronger, more resilient communities— proving that with collaboration and care, sustainable water management can lead to flourishing ecosystems and brighter futures.

## **Waste Management and Circular Economy** 

We treat waste not as a byproduct, but as a resource. From cafeteria composting to e-waste recycling, we have established clear systems to divert material from landfills and close the loop wherever possible. The entire waste generated is classified into 12 distinct categories to enable specialised treatment and material recovery. Organic Waste Converters installed at large facilities convert food and garden waste into nutrient-rich compost used for landscaping. To ensure traceability, waste handling is tracked through our internal Management Information Systems and disposal certificates are recorded and verified. 

Non-hazardous wastes are handed over for recycling and other recovery options (waste to energy). In FY 24-25, we have been able to recycle **89%** of the waste generated in our facilities, which further strengthens our Zero Waste to Landfill by 2027 goal.

## **Value creation for suppliers** 

We engage with our suppliers to ensure seamless delivery of quality products and services, uphold responsible business practices and drive shared value. A structured approach is followed to uphold integrity and responsibility across our supply chain governance practices. Our Sustainable Supply Chain Policy promotes ethical conduct, environmental responsibility and occupational health and safety, in alignment with our Supplier Code of Conduct. 

Our digital interventions such as API-integrated onboarding platform, automated email notifications and unified supplier collaboration interface have helped us in increasing effectiveness and strengthening partnerships with our suppliers.

## **Living the Code - Tata Code of Conduct** 

The Tata Code of Conduct (‘TCOC’) is the foundational framework that inspires us to conduct ourselves with the highest standards of integrity and drive our business ethically. The TCOC defines the core values and principles that guide our business practices. To ensure that its principles are understood all employees undertake a mandatory annual training through an interactive e-learning module, with new hires completing it at the time of onboarding. These are complemented by regular policy-specific training sessions led by our Legal Compliance team. Our third-party partners engage with the TCOC through structured onboarding, contractual acceptance and due diligence procedures. 



Tata Communications Limited awarded with Jagjivan Ram Award 2024 under the category of “Good Governance” at the 34<sup>th</sup> Annual Global Conclave of IISSM held in New Delhi. 

### **Compliance in Action** 

Our Compliance Certification Programme engages senior leadership in quarterly assessments of functional adherence to statutory and internal policy requirements. This certification process provides a structured oversight mechanism, ensuring that governance practices remain effective and transparent at all organisational levels. 

In FY 24-25, we introduced the Compliance Outreach Programme - quarterly sessions designed to address specific compliance areas relevant to the business functions and the responsibilities of respective functional stakeholders. These sessions strive to integrate governance principles into daily operations. 

Our Compliance framework is assessed through our annual compliance reporting exercise. The Annual Compliance Report is a detailed assessment report of our varied compliance policies and initiatives, guiding our continuous improvement in business ethics. This report evaluates our actions against the four pillars of the Leadership of Business Ethics Framework: Leadership, Compliance Structure, Communication & Training and Measurement of Effectiveness. We have consistently sustained the ‘ **<u>Advanced</u>** ’ maturity rating i.e., the highest rating achievable under this assessment. 

Beyond compliance, we also engage employees on the practical aspects of governance through initiatives such as **<u>Ethics Week</u>** and the **<u>Leadership Dialogue on Tata Values</u>** . These forums bring ethical discussions into day-to-day decisions. We also use our internal communications platforms to regularly impart knowledge and awareness concerning our policies and procedures and related insights.

# **Information Security and Data Privacy** 

We also participated in the Tata Group’s Ethics and Affirmative Action Summit 2025, contributing our learnings and gaining insights from other group companies on governance and inclusive practices. 

Data privacy and information security form an integral part of our governance framework. In FY 24-25, we strengthened this framework with a multi-tiered model focused on strategic oversight, continuous improvement and regulatory alignment. Security is embedded into enterprise risk assessments and strategic planning, supported by regular Board updates, audits, third-party reviews and automated compliance checks to ensure transparency and accountability. 



# **Cybersecurity Enhancements** 

Tata Communications strengthened its cybersecurity posture to proactively address evolving threats. Key initiatives included expanding defence mechanisms, enhancing Endpoint Detection and Response ('EDR') capabilities and integrating a robust Threat Intelligence Platform for real-time threat mitigation. We scaled our Attack Surface Management efforts to continuously identify and reduce vulnerabilities and deployed a comprehensive Vulnerability Management system to ensure timely remediation. We also successfully recertified our Information Security Management System under ISO 27001:2022, reaffirming our commitment to global best practices.

# **Regulatory Liaison and Compliance** 

We maintain an integrated regulatory function that supports compliance across jurisdictions, while participating in consultations and policy dialogues. Our teams engage directly with telecommunications, cybersecurity and data governance bodies across geographies. 

Our collaborative approach to regulatory engagement, emphasises openness, responsiveness and mutual respect. Our goal is to foster trust and ensure full compliance with applicable laws and regulations. We continue to engage meaningfully with global and domestic regulatory authorities and industry associations to align with evolving legal frameworks and support policy development that advances digital infrastructure. 

# **India Regulatory Engagements** 

India’s telecom sector operates under a complex, tightly regulated environment. We work closely with the Department of Telecommunications (‘DoT’), Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (‘TRAI’), and several Indian industry bodies to represent our business interests, ensure compliance and participate in shaping telecom reform. Through our internal compliance monitoring mechanism, we ensure timely submissions of regulatory reports and disclosures. Our participation also extends to collaborative industry initiatives focusing on AI governance, 6G research, digital infrastructure and standardisation. 

# **Global Regulatory Engagements** 

We also monitor global regulatory developments to anticipate changes and ensure that our operations remain aligned with applicable frameworks. In parallel, we are exploring the use of AI governance tools for risk assessments and mitigations and regulatory compliance to stay ahead of emerging technology challenges. 

Through forums such as the i3Forum’s One Consortium and the Global Informal Regulatory Antifraud Forum ('GIRAF'), we collaborate with other global players to improve practices around robocalling mitigation, digital fraud prevention and policy harmonisation. In the U.S., we are contributing to ongoing discussions around submarine cable licensing. In Saudi Arabia, we completed a regulatory sandbox, showcasing our connected car technology and continue engagement on new licensing models.

Mr. N. Ganapathy Subramaniam<br>Chairman and Non-Executive Director<br><!-- End of picture text -->

Mr. N. Ganapathy Subramaniam was the Chief Operating Officer (‘COO’) and Executive Director of Tata Consultancy Services Limited (‘TCS’) since February 2017 till May 2024. He joined the Board of Tata Communications on December 2, 2021 and became the Chairman on March 14, 2025. He is also a Director and Chairman of Tata Elxsi Limited and Tejas Networks Limited. He has over 40 years of experience in TCS in strategic management of technology and operations, across large corporations in both established and new growth markets. He has played a strategic role in several landmark initiatives that TCS undertook across banking, telecom and public services globally. He has also been part of the evolution of Indian IT industry, and the value creation process with a globally distributed talent. His indepth knowledge of technology, operations, product development, business transformation and change management as organisations manage their technology and business.

He is a global technocommercial leader across regions and industries recognised for developing scalable businesses in UK, Europe, Japan and India, and has worked across the globe Under his leadership, Tata Communications is progressing to play a solid role as a digital fabric on which customers can build secure, connected, digital experiences. NOTICE is hereby given that the 39<sup>th</sup> Annual General Meeting of Tata Communications Limited (‘Company’) will be held at 11:00 a.m. (IST) on Wednesday, July 9, 2025, through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual Means to transact the following business: 

### **Ordinary Business** 

##### **1. Adoption of Audited Standalone Financial Statements** 

To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Standalone Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 together with the Reports of the Board of Directors and the Auditors thereon. 

##### **2. Adoption of Audited Consolidated Financial Statements** 

To receive, consider and adopt the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2025 together with the Report of the Auditors thereon. 

##### **3. Declaration of Dividend** 

To declare a dividend on equity shares of the Company 

for the financial year ended March 31, 2025. 

##### **4. Appointment of Mr. Ankur Verma (DIN: 07972892) as Director, liable to retire by rotation** 

To appoint a Director in place of Mr. Ankur Verma 

(DIN: 07972892), who retires by rotation and being eligible, offers himself for re-appointment. 

### **Special Business** 

##### **5. Appointment of Secretarial Auditors and fixing their remuneration** 

To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following 

##### resolution as an **Ordinary Resolution** : 

“ **RESOLVED THAT** pursuant to the provisions of Section 204 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) read with the Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014 and Regulation 24A of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (‘SEBI Listing Regulations’) [including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof for the time being in force], M/s. Parikh & Associates, Company Secretaries in Practice (Firm Registration No. P1988MH009800), who have confirmed their eligibility to be appointed as the Secretarial Auditors of the Company in terms of Regulation 24A (1A) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, be and are hereby appointed as the Secretarial Auditors of the Company, for a term of five consecutive years, commencing from financial year 2025-26 till financial year 2029-30.” 

“ **RESOLVED FURTHER THAT** the Board of Directors 

of the Company be and is hereby authorised to fix the annual remuneration plus applicable taxes and out-ofpocket expenses payable to M/s. Parikh & Associates during their tenure as the Secretarial Auditors of the Company.” 

“ **RESOLVED FURTHER THAT** the Board of Directors (which term shall be deemed to include any committee of the Board constituted to exercise its powers, including the powers conferred by this Resolution) and the Company Secretary of the Company, be and are hereby severally authorised to do such acts, deeds and things as may be required and take all such steps as may be necessary, proper and expedient to give effect to this Resolution.” 

##### **6. Ratification of Cost Auditor’s Remuneration** 

To consider and, if thought fit, to pass the following resolution as an **Ordinary Resolution** : 

“ **RESOLVED THAT** pursuant to the provisions of Section 148 and other applicable provisions, if any, of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 [including any statutory modification(s) or re-enactment(s) thereof for the time being in force], the Company hereby ratifies the remuneration of `H` 6.60 lakhs plus applicable taxes and out-of-pocket expenses on actual basis incurred in connection with the audit, capped at 3% of the remuneration, payable to Ms. Ketki D. Visariya, Cost Accountant (Membership No.: 16028), who, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, has been appointed by the Board of Directors as the Cost Auditor of the Company, to conduct the audit of the cost records maintained by the Company for the financial year 2025-26.” 

“ **RESOLVED FURTHER THAT** the Board of Directors (which term shall be deemed to include any committee of the Board constituted to exercise its powers, including the powers conferred by this Resolution) and the Company Secretary of the Company, be and are hereby severally authorised to do such acts, deeds and things as may be required and take all such steps as may be necessary, proper and expedient to give effect to this Resolution.”

The e-Voting module shall be disabled by NSDL for voting 15 minutes after the conclusion of the AGM. 

28. The Scrutinizer shall, immediately after the conclusion of voting at the Meeting, first count the votes cast during the AGM, thereafter, unblock the votes cast through remote e-Voting and make, not later than two working days from the conclusion of the AGM, a consolidated Scrutinizer’s Report of the total votes cast in favour or against, if any, to the Chairperson or a person authorised by the Chairperson in writing, who shall countersign the same. 

29. The Company shall simultaneously forward the results to BSE Limited and National Stock Exchange of India Limited, where the shares of the Company are listed. ## **In respect of Item No. 5** 

with the conditions prescribed under Regulation 24A (1A) of the SEBI Listing Regulations. 

As per the provisions of Section 204 of the Act and Regulation 24A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Company is required to undertake Secretarial Audit by a Secretarial Auditor who shall be a Peer Reviewed Company Secretary. Regulation 24A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, as amended, further requires the Company to obtain the approval of its Members for appointment or re-appointment of the Secretarial Auditors. 

The fee proposed to be paid to M/s. Parikh & Associates towards Secretarial Audit for FY 2025-26 shall be `H` 2.50 lakhs per annuam (with an increase of 10% after every 2 years), excluding applicable taxes and out of pocket expenses, with the authority to the Board to make revisions as it may deem fit. There is no material change in the proposed fee payable to M/s. Parikh & Associates compared to that of the previous Secretarial Auditor. 

The Board of Directors of the Company (‘Board’) at its meeting held on April 22, 2025 appointed M/s. Parikh & Associates, Peer Reviewed Firm of Company Secretaries in Practice (Firm Registration No. P1988MH009800 / Peer Review No. 6556/2025), as the Secretarial Auditor of the Company for a term of five consecutive years, commencing from financial year 2025-26 till financial year 2029-30, subject to approval of the Members. If appointed, M/s. Parikh & Associates will carry out Secretarial Audit for financial years 2025-26 to 2029-30. M/s. Parikh & Associates have submitted their eligibility certificate and consent to act as the Secretarial Auditor of the Company and have confirmed that their proposed appointment, if made, will be in accordance 

The fee for services in the nature of statutory certifications and other permissible non-audit services will be in addition to the secretarial audit fee as above, and will be decided by the Management in consultation with the Secretarial Auditors. The provision of such permissible non-audit services will be reviewed and approved by the Board. 

M/s. Parikh & Associates is a well-known firm of Practising Company Secretaries founded in 1987 and based in Mumbai. Renowned for its commitment to quality and precision, the firm has been Peer Reviewed and Quality Reviewed by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, ensuring the

# **In respect of Item No. 6** 

Under the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, as amended, the Company is required to have the audit of its cost records conducted by a Cost Accountant. Further, in accordance with the provisions of Section 148 of the Act read with the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor has to be ratified by the Members of the Company. 

The Board, on the recommendation of the Audit Committee, has approved the appointment and remuneration of Ms. Ketki D. Visariya, Cost Accountant, as Cost Auditor to conduct the audit of the cost records of the Company for the financial year ending March 31, 2026. Accordingly, under the approval from the Board of Directors, the remuneration of the Cost Auditor was fixed at `H` 6.60 lakhs plus applicable taxes and out of pocket expenses on actual basis capped at 3% of the remuneration. 

Accordingly, consent of the Members is sought by way of an Ordinary Resolution as set out at Item No. 6 of the accompanying Notice for ratification of the remuneration payable to the Cost Auditor for the financial year ending March 31, 2026. 

The Board recommends the Ordinary Resolution set out at Item No. 6 of the Notice for approval by the Members. 

None of the Directors and KMPs or their relatives are concerned or interested in the Resolution at Item No. 6 of the accompanying Notice. 

# **In respect of Item No. 7** 

Based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and after obtaining necessary security clearance under the Company’s TV uplinking license from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the Board of Directors appointed Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma (DIN: 09075212), as an Additional Director (in the capacity of Independent Director), to hold office for a term of five consecutive years 



i.e., with effect from April 22, 2025 up to April 21, 2030 (both days inclusive), pursuant to the provisions of Sections 149, 150 and 152 read with Schedule IV to the Act and the Articles of Association of the Company. 

Pursuant to Regulation 17(1C) of the SEBI Listing Regulations, a director shall hold office until the date of next General Meeting or for a period of three months from the date of appointment, whichever is earlier. The Company has received notice under section 160 of the Act proposing his candidature as an Independent Director of the Company. If appointed, Mr. Varma will act as a Non-Executive, Independent Director, not liable to retire by rotation. 

The Company has received a declaration from Mr. Varma stating that he meets the criteria as provided under section 149(6) read with section 149(7) of the Act, Regulation 16(1)(b) read with Regulation 25(8) of the SEBI Listing Regulations. Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma has also given a declaration that he is not disqualified under section 164 of the Act nor debarred from holding the office of a director by virtue of any order pass by SEBI or any other authority and has registered himself in the Independent Director’s Data Bank maintained by Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs. 

In the opinion of the Board, Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma is independent of the Management of the Company and is a person of integrity and possesses relevant expertise and experience and fulfils the conditions for appointment as an Independent Director as specified in the Act and the SEBI Listing Regulations and any modification(s) / amendment(s) thereto. 

The terms and conditions of his appointment as an Independent Director shall be open for inspection by the Members. 

Keeping in view his experience and expertise, the Special Resolution at Item No. 7 of the accompanying Notice for his appointment as an Independent Director of the Company is in the interest of the Company and is recommended by the Board for approval by the Members. The Board is satisfied that the appointment of Mr. Varma is justified on account of his educational background and rich professional experience in the areas of Finance, Banking, Risk Management and Compliance. 

None of the other Directors or KMPs or their relatives except Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma is concerned or interested in the Resolution set out at Item No. 7 of the accompanying Notice. 

## <u>Brief profile of Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma:</u> 

Mr. Sujit Kumar Varma is a career banker with proven track record of leading diverse business departments. Mr. Varma is highly experienced in Corporate and Retail Credit, Trade Finance, International Banking, Risk Management and Compliance. Mr. Varma had been associated with the State Bank of India (“SBI”) for over 30 years where he held several important positions viz., Chief Executive Officer - SBI New York USA, General Manager - Mid-Corporate Regional Office, Mumbai, India and Chief General Manager - International Banking. Mr. Varma superannuated as Deputy Managing Director, Corporate Accounts Group from SBI in January 2021. 

Mr. Varma holds a Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) in English and certifications from renowned institutes like Indian Institute of Banking & Finance, Mumbai, India; Harvard Business School; NYU Stern School of Business, New York, USA; Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, India and Indian Institute of Management, Calcutta, India.

<u>Brief profile of Mr. P. Jagdish Rao:</u> 

Mr. P. Jagdish Rao, aged 65 years, is a seasoned financial services and technology executive with over 35 years of experience at Citibank and Citigroup, where he played a pivotal role in driving large-scale business transformations, optimising global banking operations, and implementing advanced technology platforms. He has deep expertise in cyber security, data analytics and corporate governance, having interacted extensively with the Citigroup Board for 20 years. In his leadership roles, he managed technology infrastructure, corporate realty services and business operations worldwide. Mr. Rao spearheaded several strategic transformation initiatives such as consolidating Citi’s global data centers, cutting IT costs by over US$2 billion and implementing Citi’s Private Cloud infrastructure, which helped enhance digital and mobile banking capabilities. He also led the consolidation of Citigroup’s global real estate footprint, reducing it by over 60%, resulting in significant cost savings. 

Throughout his career, Mr. Rao has held various senior leadership positions, including Chairman of Citigroup Technology Inc., Chief Administrative Officer for the Global Consumer Bank and twice serving as Citigroup’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). He has extensive experience in mergers and acquisitions, divesting several Citi subsidiaries globally and managing corporate operations across diverse regions such as Asia, Europe, Latin America and the U.S. His earlier career included roles in corporate banking, treasury and trade services, and transaction banking. With a strong educational foundation in engineering and business, Mr. Rao is recognised for his ability to lead and implement large-scale global transformations that align technology with business goals. 

Mr. Rao is a graduate engineer in Electronics & Electrical Communication Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (1981) and has an MBA from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (1984). He has also completed the Advanced Management Program at Kellogg Business School, North Western University, Evanston, IL. 

He is a US citizen residing in New York City.

## **Company’s Performance** 

FY 2024-25 was a year of steady and sustained growth for Tata Communications, against the backdrop of ongoing global macroeconomic challenges. The Company continued to build momentum in the digital portfolio, which recorded a 29.5% yearon-year growth and now constitutes nearly half of the overall revenues. This performance emphasises the growing relevance of our digital fabric strategy encompassing Network, Cloud, IoT, and Interaction fabrics. The order book and deal pipeline remain healthy, supported by large, multi-fabric wins across diverse geographies and industry verticals. 

During the year, the Company took several strategic initiatives, including the monetisation of a large land parcel at Ambattur, Chennai and divestment of non-core subsidiaries such as Tata Communications Payment Solutions Limited. We have sharpened capital allocation and positioned the Company to prioritise investment in core business areas. 



As we enter FY 2025-26, Tata Communications is wellpositioned with a sharpened strategic focus, continued digital growth, and a roadmap for delivering sustainable, long-term value. 

On a standalone basis, the revenue from operations for FY 2024-25 was `H` 7,277.86 crore, lower by 8.93% over the previous year’s revenue of `H` 7,991.68 crore. The profit after tax (‘PAT’) attributable to shareholders for FY 2024-25 was `H` 1,050.87 crore as compared to PAT of `H` 638.63 crore for the previous year. These changes reflect the impact of the hiveoff of the Company’s new-edged digital services business to Novamesh Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company at the start of the financial year. The increase in PAT is additionally attributable to the exceptional income from land monetisation during the year. 

On a consolidated basis, the revenue from operations for FY 2024-25 was `H` 23,108.59 crore, higher by 11.18% over the previous year’s revenue of `H` 20,784.68 crore. The PAT attributable to shareholders and non-controlling interests for FY 2024-25 was `H` 1,836.78 crore as compared to `H` 969.58 crore for the previous year. The growth in consolidated revenue is driven by additional revenue and synergies from the entities acquired during the previous financial year, gain on land monetisation and strategic divestment of Tata Communications Payment Solutions Limited by the Company during the year. 

## **Dividend** 

The Board recommends a dividend of `H` 25/- per fully paid equity share on 285,000,000 equity shares of face value `H` 10/- each, for the financial year ended March 31, 2025. The Board has recommended dividend based on the parameters laid down in the Dividend Distribution Policy, which can be accessed at - <u>www.tatacommunications.com/resource/corporate resources/policies/tcl-dividend-distribution-policy/.</u> 

The dividend on equity shares is subject to approval of the Members at the Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’) scheduled to be held on Wednesday, July 9, 2025. 

The dividend, once approved by the Members, will be paid, subject to deduction of tax at source, on or after Thursday, July 10, 2025. If approved, the dividend will result in a cash outflow of `H` 712.5 crore. The dividend on equity shares is 250% of the paid-up value of each share. The total dividend pay-out works out to 38.79% of the consolidated profit after tax attributable to shareholders and non-controlling interest for FY 2024-25. 

The Company has fixed Thursday, June 19, 2025 as the ‘Record Date’ and will close the Register of Members from Friday, June 20, 2025 till Monday, June 23, 2025 (both days inclusive) for determining entitlement of Members to final dividend for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, if approved at the AGM. 

## **Share Capital** 

As on March 31, 2025, the authorised share capital of the Company consisted of 400,000,000 equity shares of `H` 10/- 

each, and the paid-up equity share capital consisted of 285,000,000 equity shares of `H` 10/- each. During FY 2024-25, the Company has not issued any shares, securities / instruments convertible into equity shares, sweat equity shares or shares with differential voting rights. 

The Members, at the 37<sup>th</sup> AGM, vide special resolution approved ‘Tata Communications Limited - Employee Stock Unit Plan 2023’ (‘Plan’) to create, offer, issue, grant and allot from time to time, in one or more tranches, up to 30,00,000 (Thirty Lakh) employee stock units (‘RSUs’) to eligible employees of the Company. The Plan has been formulated in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (‘Act’) and SEBI (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021 (‘SBEB Regulations’). The Nomination and Remuneration Committee (‘NRC’) administers the Plan and functions as the Compensation Committee for the purposes of SBEB Regulations. 

The statutory disclosures as mandated under the SBEB Regulations and a certificate from the Secretarial Auditor confirming implementation of the above-mentioned Plan in accordance with SBEB Regulations and Members’ approval, is hosted on the website of the Company at <u>https://www. tatacommunications.com/investors/results/.</u> Eligible employees shall be granted RSUs, as determined by the NRC, which will vest as per the approved vesting schedule and are exercisable into fully paid-up equity shares of `H` 10/-<sup>each of the Company, on the terms and</sup> conditions as provided under the Plan, in accordance with the provisions
